newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hog prices seen steady-off $0.50- trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by packer resistance to recent price gains which have pushed operating margins into unprofitable territory, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $58.00 to $58.50, the same as Tuesday's top but up $1.00 from Friday's top.
Illinois top prices at plants were seen ranging from $57.50 to $58.00 and Indiana/Ohio tops at plants were seen at $57.00 to $57.50, dealers in those areas said.
Packer competition for hogs to fill previously booked pork orders lifted prices in the direct market early this week as did light movement, the dealers said.
Demand for hogs also was tied to moderate pork sales at mostly higher prices, they said.
Pork prices at midday were quoted mostly $2.00 per cwt higher for bellies and steady to up $3.00 for lean trimmings, while hams were generally $1.00 lower, USDA said.
There were 45.0 pork loads and 24.0 loads of pork trimmings sold.
